tutorial.welcomeBody: We can show you how club finances work, including balance, sponsors, transactions, taxes, and team policies.
tutorial.overviewBody:
This is the Finance page.

The Overview tab shows the main financial situation of your club, including current balance, income, expenses, cashflow, and financial summaries.

If your team has emergency debt or financial problems, this is where you can quickly understand the current situation.
tutorial.sponsorsBody:
The Sponsors tab shows the sponsors your team has already signed.

Sponsors can bring money to the club, but they may also have targets or bonus objectives. These targets explain what your team needs to achieve and how much money you can receive.

Sponsor contracts can be standard contracts or naming-rights contracts. A standard sponsor contract gives your club sponsor money without changing your team name.

A naming-rights contract is usually worth more money, but the sponsor name becomes part of your team name during the season. At the beginning of the next season, your original team name returns.

If your team does not have a sponsor yet, you can use the sponsor offers area to look for new deals.
tutorial.transactionsBody:
The Transactions tab shows your club’s financial history.

Here you can see income and expenses during the season, including prize money, sponsor payments, salaries, transfers, infrastructure costs, equipment purchases, training camps, tax withdrawals, and other financial movements.
tutorial.taxBody:
The Tax tab shows your club’s tax situation.

Transactions can create tax obligations, and a tax audit happens once per month. This page helps you see how much tax has been calculated, what has already been paid, and what still needs to be paid.
tutorial.policiesBody:
Team Policies and Operations control how your club is run.

Changing policies can make your club more attractive to riders and staff, but it can also increase the cost of travel, race support, training camps, and daily operations.

This section helps you balance comfort, performance, attractiveness, and cost.

After Finance, the next tutorial will explain the main Menu.
